releases.name: v0.1.13 — scrollbox and borders
releases.body:
## A panel that behaves like a window

0.1.13 turns the todo panel into a scrollable, bordered window.

- **Rounded border** everywhere: the list, the editor, the settings and the help dialogs. `borderStyle` in the settings
  switches it between `rounded`, `single` and `none`; the list border turns red while a delete is armed and cyan while
  the search owns the keyboard.
- **Scrolling instead of paging**: the cursor moves over every task and the view follows it. `PgUp`/`PgDn`,
  `Home`/`End` and the arrows move the cursor; the footer shows `position/rows`.
- **Settings clean-up**: values are clipped to their column, `Save to` shows `global` or `project` instead of a long
  path, and the dialog re-centres itself after mounting.
- **`borderStyle` setting**, documented with the rest.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

## Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

61 unit tests. MIT.

## What's new in 0.1.13- Rounded borders on the list, the editor, the settings and the help; `borderStyle` picks `rounded`, `single` or `none`.
- The border turns red while a delete is armed, and cyan while the search box has the keyboard.
- The list scrolls instead of paging: the cursor walks every task and the view follows it.
- Settings values are clipped to their column, `Save to` shows `global` or `project`, and the dialog centres itself at mount.

releases.name: v0.1.12 — settings and compact help
releases.body:
## Settings, compact help, honest docs

**`/todo settings`** has 17 options, saved to `~/.config/opencode/todo-md.json` or to the project's
`.opencode/todo-md.json`. The dialog works on a draft: **Save** writes, **Cancel**/`Esc` discards, **Reset to
defaults** restores, **Export/Import JSON** move the whole set through a file. Values are right-aligned and the dialog
uses the same colours as the screenshot. It also opens from the `Settings ▸` row in the todo panel.

**Shortcut bar** is one compact line at the bottom; clicking it opens the full key list. The `showHints` setting turns
it off, and `ctrl+d twice deletes` is back in the hint.

**Help cannot lie any more**: the key list is generated from `SHORTCUTS`, and a test compares it against the bindings
actually registered in the panel, both directions. Titles are short enough that nothing overflows the dialog.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

## Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

61 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.11 — settings and column colours
releases.body:
## Settings, colours, and a crash fix

`/todo settings` opens a dialog that works on a draft: **Save** writes it, **Cancel**/`Esc` drops it. Each row cycles its value on click, `Reset to defaults` restores everything (keeping the target), and **Export JSON** / **Import JSON** move the whole set through a file.

Settings live in `~/.config/opencode/todo-md.json` (global) and `<project>/.opencode/todo-md.json` (project wins); `Save to` chooses which file Save writes.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

## New in 0.1.11

- 17 settings: padding, palette, hidden columns (created/done/tag), description width, strip width and collapse threshold, completed tasks in the strip, coloured strip header, rows per page, start filter and sort, delete mode, renumber after done, auto-create TODO.md, Save to
- `Settings ▸` in the todo dialog opens the settings directly
- Per-column colours, from the theme (`theme`) or the Catppuccin palette used in the screenshots (`fixed`)
- Configurable inner padding
- Fix a crash at render time: `visibleColumn` used `settings` from outside its scope, which `bun build` cannot catch

## Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

60 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.10 — plugin load fix
releases.body:
## The plugin loads again

0.1.8 shipped a broken import: `src/index.ts` used `TODO_STATUSES` and `TODO_PRIORITIES` without importing them, so the plugin failed to load with:

```
ReferenceError: TODO_STATUSES is not defined
failed to load plugin
```

No tool was registered at all — `todo_write` and `todo_read` simply did not exist. Fixed in 0.1.10.

> Note: 0.1.9 never reached the registry (it stayed as a staged publish and cannot be promoted), so this is 0.1.10 with the same fix.

![The /todo dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonVeganMan/opencode-todo-md/master/screen/todo.png)

## Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

## Recap of recent versions

- 0.1.10 — fix the load failure, the plugin registers its tools again
- 0.1.8 — `todo_write` merges by default: items without an `id` are appended, items with an `id` are updated; `mode: "replace"` is the only way to delete tasks
- 0.1.7 — `/todo renumber`, ids rewritten 1..N by priority and due date
- 0.1.6 / 0.1.5 — `ctrl+n` creates a task, `ctrl+e` opens the selected task in the editor

58 unit tests. MIT.

releases.name: v0.1.9 — plugin load fix
releases.body:
## Plugin did not load at all

0.1.8 declared the tool input schema with `TODO_STATUSES` and `TODO_PRIORITIES` but never imported them, so the server half threw on load:

```
ReferenceError: TODO_STATUSES is not defined
failed to load plugin target=...opencode-todo-md
```

No tools were registered: `todo_write` and `todo_read` were simply missing. 0.1.9 imports both constants.

### Install

```json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-todo-md"] }
```

The TUI half (sidebar strip and `/todo`) loads at TUI startup: restart `opencode`, or run `/reload`.

### Everything from 0.1.8 is included

- `todo_write` merges by default: items without an `id` are appended, items with an `id` are updated.
- `mode: "replace"` is the only way to delete tasks; an empty list clears the file.
- Stable ids, priorities, due dates, completion dates, tags, `/todo renumber`, `/todo import`.

58 unit tests. MIT.
